asks: The Edmonton-City Centre MLA supports the interim Edmonton-City Centre boundaries and the added Edmonton seat, and asks the commission to consider growth in the core and possibly another Edmonton seat.

The mayor of Leduc County asks to keep Leduc-Beaumont as it is with all of Beaumont, not to put pieces of Leduc County into Strathcona-Sherwood Park or Camrose, to extend Stony Plain-Drayton Valley-Devon to Highway 814, and to put Pigeon Lake under one MLA.
A Crawford Plains resident asks that south-east Edmonton ridings respect the Anthony Henday as a community divide and that ridings get place names rather than compass names; no specific map offered.
An Edmonton housing consultant asks the commission to keep six urban-centre Edmonton ridings rather than five and cautions against hybrid ridings in general.
A Ritchie resident asks the commission to keep six Edmonton core ridings and to move the Edmonton-Strathcona boundary from 99th Street to Mill Creek ravine so Ritchie is not divided.
A Strathcona-Sherwood Park resident asks to keep Heritage Hills in Strathcona-Sherwood Park, not to add part of Beaumont, and to use Wye Road as the southern boundary.
An Edmonton-City Centre resident asks for Edmonton ridings that extend beyond city limits into nearby communities such as Devon, Beaumont and Spruce Grove (more of Beaumont with Edmonton-Ellerslie).

quote: communities like Sherwood Park, St. Albert, Devon, Beaumont were separate towns with separate identities
note: St. Albert named only as an example of a once-separate town near Edmonton; her named targets for Edmonton hybrids are Devon, Beaumont and Spruce Grove. Mention, no stance (rule 6).

asks: A Beverly-Clareview resident supports the interim Edmonton-Beverly-Clareview boundaries, including adding Fraser and Kirkness and moving Belvedere to Edmonton-Decore.
A St. Albert resident speaking about Edmonton asks the commission to keep Edmonton-Riverview as a distinct riding rather than dissolve it.

note: Presenter says he lives in St. Albert; speaks only about Edmonton-Riverview. Mention, no stance.

asks: An Edmonton-McClung resident asks that the number of eligible voters (citizens), not total population, be used to draw ridings.

note: Airdrie-Cochrane cited only as the riding with the most registered voters in a statistics argument. Mention, no stance (rule 6).
Airdrie-Cochrane cited only as a voter-count statistic. Mention, no stance.
Lesser Slave Lake cited only for its registered-voter count and deviation. Mention, no stance.

asks: A presenter asks that Devon be placed in Edmonton-South West rather than in a rural or Edmonton-West Enoch district.
no request (an audience member from Devon answers commissioners' questions about how many Devon residents work in Nisku).

The reeve of Clearwater County asks the commission to keep Clearwater County within a single electoral division rather than divide it among Banff-Jasper, Mountain View-Kneehill and Lacombe-Rocky Mountain House.

quote: Clearwater county respectfully urges the commission to reconsider boundary options to maintain Clearwater county within a single provincial electoral division wherever possible.
note: No EB label precedes the quote in this record (follows EB-720). Rejection words: 'the proposal would fragment the county across multiple ridings, including the proposed Banff-Jasper, Mountain View-Kneehill, and Lacombe-Rocky Mountain House electoral divisions'. Says nothing about what else should share the district, so W0 rather than W1; refers to its 'longstanding representation within one single riding'.

Names the interim Banff-Jasper only as one of the districts receiving part of Clearwater County; objects to the split, says nothing for or against park or Bighorn lands with Rocky Mountain House. Mention, no stance (rule 17).
Names Mountain View-Kneehill only as receiving part of Clearwater County; nothing about Sundre or the Rocky View towns. Mention, no stance.

asks: A Strathcona-Sherwood Park resident asks to keep Heritage Hills in the riding and not to add part of Beaumont; if population must be added, add Tofield.

A Ritchie resident asks for two additional Edmonton ridings, no removal of a central Edmonton district, little weight on proximity to the Legislature, and Mill Creek ravine as the Edmonton-Strathcona boundary.

A Sherwood Park resident asks to return Heritage Hills to Strathcona-Sherwood Park and, if Sherwood Park needs population, to add rural Strathcona County north of Highway 16 up to Fort Saskatchewan and Josephburg; also says splitting Beaumont is ludicrous.
A resident north of Highway 16 asks that her rural Strathcona County area be moved from Fort Saskatchewan-Vegreville into the Sherwood Park riding.

The CAO of Forestburg asks to move Forestburg, Alliance and the area south of Township Road 430 (and possibly Heisler) from Camrose to Drumheller-Stettler, and questions moving Hardisty to Drumheller-Stettler.

Public Interest Alberta asks the commission to keep six central Edmonton ridings, to use hybrids sparingly, to keep Ritchie and Hazeldean in Edmonton-Strathcona, and favours a tighter population variance.
A resident of Edmonton-Strathcona asks the commission to give inner-city Calgary and Edmonton ridings fair representation that recognizes their density and future growth.

An Edmonton-Gold Bar constituency staffer asks the commission not to merge Edmonton-Glenora and Edmonton-Riverview, to add Edmonton seats, not to put part of Beaumont in Strathcona-Sherwood Park, and to account for Sherwood Park growth.
